record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the same problem (III) in the regime k−α<1, do compact-support solutions exist at all?

evidence.quote: it would be interesting to know if there is more than one positive solution in the first case k − α < 1 and if, also in this case, there are compact support solutions. Information on the structure of the set of compact support solutions is interesting as well.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\ge 1$) be a bounded smooth domain containing the origin, and let $k\ge 0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$ be real parameters. Consider the singular semilinear elliptic problem with absorption

$$
\text{(III)}\qquad
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u + |x|^{k}\, u^{-\alpha}\,\chi_{\{u>0\}} \;=\; \lambda\, u & \text{in } \Omega,\\[2pt]
u\ge 0 & \text{in } \Omega,\\[2pt]
u = 0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega,
\end{cases}
$$

where $\lambda>0$ is a parameter and $\chi_{\{u>0\}}$ is the characteristic function of the set on which $u$ is positive (so that the absorption term $|x|^{k}u^{-\alpha}$ is defined only where $u>0$ and is set to $0$ where $u=0$). By a solution one means a nonnegative function $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfying the equation in the sense of distributions on $\Omega$.

A solution $u$ is said to have *compact support* if the set $\{x\in\Omega:u(x)>0\}$ is compactly contained in $\Omega$; equivalently, $u$ vanishes identically on a neighborhood of $\partial\Omega$, producing a free boundary $\partial\{u>0\}\subset\Omega$.

Question: In the parameter regime $k-\alpha<1$, do there exist compact‑support solutions of problem (III)? If so, describe the structure of the set of such compact‑support solutions (e.g., multiplicity, monotonicity in $\lambda$, dependence on $\Omega$).

artifact.status_search_result: The survey explicitly lists the existence and structure of compact-support solutions in the regime k − α < 1 as an open question. No subsequent publication addressing this specific regime for problem (III) was located through web search; related works on branches of positive and free boundary solutions to singular quasilinear problems exist but do not resolve this case.
